newsitem.title: CAMEROON: Cameroon hands back ex-president's seized property.
newsitem.headline: Cameroon hands back ex-president's seized property.

text.p: The Cameroon authorities have begun returning to the family of independence president Ahmadou Ahidjo property seized after a coup attempt against president Paul Biya in 1983, Ahidjo's son said.
Mahamadou Ahidjo, mayor of Garoua in the north and himself an opposition activist, said an initial handover ceremony took place in the town at the weekend.

"This is all my father's property which he legally acquired and I see no reason why handing it over should attract media publicity," he told Reuters by telephone, denouncing the use state media were making of the handover.

Ahidjo, a northerner elected president when French Cameroon became independent in 1960, became president of present-day Cameroon a year later when part of British Cameroon rallied to the new republic.

He resigned on grounds of ill-health in 1982 and handed power to Biya but was sentenced to death in absentia on charges of complicity in the coup attempt. Biya commuted the sentence to life imprisonment. Ahidjo died in exile in Senegal in 1989.

"A committee has been set up by the government to identify and subsequently hand over all the property of former president Ahmadou Ahidjo to his family as soon as possible," a government statement said.
The property includes 25 buildings which have already been handed over.
